description: CODEVERSE is a technology-driven team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We aim to develop a scientific data platform that explores NASA Earth observation datasets, identifies environmental trends, evaluates statistical significance, and communicates insights through interactive maps and visualizations. We're passionate about AI/ML and solving real-world challenges. We're looking for collaborators skilled in Earth science, data analysis, visualization and web development.
summary:
TerraTrend is an interactive Earth-system trend exploration platform developed by CODEVERSE'26 for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 - “Be an Earth System Trend Detective.”

Using historical environmental data from NASA POWER,TerraTrend enables users to explore changes at selected locations and across regional grid cells.It supports variables including near surface temperature,maximum and minimum temperature,precipitation,wind speed,relative humidity and surface solar irradiance.

The platform visualizes temporal patterns and geographic trends, estimates trend magnitude using Sen's slope, and evaluates monotonic trends using Mann-Kendall statistics. Regional analysis also incorporates Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate filtering to help interpret multiple grid-cell comparisons.

TerraTrend helps users investigate what is changing, where it is changing, how much it is changing, and whether statistical evidence supports the observed trend. It is designed as an exploratory tool for students, educators and researchers, not as an operational forecast or an official NASA product.
details:
Overview

TerraTrend is a NASA data-driven Earth-system trend exploration platform built to make historical environmental changes easier to investigate, visualize and interpret.

How it works

The application combines a Next.js frontend with a Python FastAPI backend. Users can select environmental variables and locations, explore historical time-series behaviour, and inspect regional grid-cell trends through interactive charts and geographic maps.

The platform supports seven environmental variables:

  • Temperature at 2 metres (T2M)
  • Maximum temperature (T2M_MAX)
  • Minimum temperature (T2M_MIN)
  • Corrected precipitation (PRECTOTCORR)
  • Wind speed at 10 metres (WS10M)
  • Surface solar downward irradiance (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN)
  • Relative humidity at 2 metres (RH2M)

Historical data are accessed through the NASA POWER Monthly and Annual API. Meteorological variables primarily use NASA GMAO MERRA-2 data, while solar radiation products have their own NASA source lineage, including CERES and related radiation datasets.

Scientific analysis

The Python analysis engine uses:

  • Sen's slope estimation to quantify trend magnitude.
  • Mann-Kendall statistical testing to evaluate monotonic trends.
  • Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate control for regional multiple-grid-cell analysis.
  • Data cleaning and missing-value handling before statistical computation.

Results are presented through time-series charts, regional maps and statistical indicators.

Technology stack

Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS.

Visualization: Recharts, Leaflet and React Leaflet.

Backend: Python, FastAPI and Pydantic.

Scientific computing: NumPy, pandas, SciPy and pyMannKendall.

Intended impact

TerraTrend aims to make Earth-system data exploration more accessible to students, educators, researchers and people interested in environmental change. It provides a common interface to investigate the direction, magnitude, geographic distribution and statistical evidence of historical environmental trends.

Limitations and scientific transparency

TerraTrend is an exploratory research and educational prototype. NASA POWER products have their own spatial resolutions, temporal coverage and uncertainties. Regional rectangular selections should not be interpreted as exact administrative boundaries, and estimated trends should not automatically be interpreted as causal relationships or forecasts.

Use of AI tools

AI-assisted tools, including ChatGPT, OpenAI Codex and Google Antigravity, were used during software development for coding assistance, debugging, documentation and technical review. The team reviewed and integrated the resulting work. Environmental observations and data values are sourced from NASA POWER; they are not AI-generated.
